title: AI-assisted multimodal differential diagnosis in diseases with myocardial thickening
summary:
Various heart diseases are associated with thickening of the
heart muscle (left ventricular myocardial hypertrophy). However, distinguishing between them poses a challenge in everyday clinical practice. At the same time, specific and effective therapies are available for many of these diseases, which is why early diagnosis is crucial to improving the prognosis for the patients. To optimize early diagnosis, diagnostic techniques that use artificial intelligence (AI) are becoming increasingly important. In this study, we therefore want to examine how well such new diagnostic techniques can detect and differentiate between heart diseases involving thickening of the heart muscle and whether they enable early and reliable diagnosis. Within this framework, the performance and benefits of an AI-supported software (Us2.ai) for detecting cardiac amyloidosis using cardiac ultrasound (echocardiography) will also be investigated. Us2.ai is approved as a tested medical device for clinical use and enables automated analysis of echocardiography images. The software can not only precisely determine various measurements (e.g., heart wall thickness), but also directly assess the probability of a specific heart disease, such as cardiac amyloidosis. Cardiac amyloidosis is a disease in which misfolded proteins are deposited in the heart, leading to thickening and stiffening of the heart muscle. In the long term, this can lead to increasing heart failure and further complications such as cardiac arrhythmia. To diagnose the disease, an MRI of the heart, a scintigraphy, or a tissue sample from the heart (biopsy) is required. These examinations are time-consuming and costly, and are not widely available. With our project, we therefore want to investigate whether the use of AI in echocardiography is suitable for accelerating the detection of cardiac amyloidosis, improving the accuracy of diagnostics, and reducing the health economic burden.

interventions.name:
Phase 1 (retrospective phase):
Retrospektive analysis of already collected clinical data and imaging data from patients with echocardiographically documented left ventricular myocardial hypertrophy from the period 2010 to 2025 using AI-assisted analysis tools (EchoNet-LVH, AI-ECG, AI-Hemodynamics).

Phase 2 (prospective phase): 
Consecutive recruitment of 110 patients with the highest us2.ai-based probability of cardiac amyloidosis from phase 1 who have not yet undergone  further cardiac amyloidosis diagnostics. These patients will be contacted by telephone and, if they consent to participate

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Phase 1 (retrospective phase):
- Echocardiographically documented left ventricular hypertrophy (wall thickness ≥13 mm)
- Digital availability of image data (echocardiography, ECG, MRI if applicable)
- Complete echocardiography series available and us2.ai software compatibility

Phase 2 (prospective phase):
- Adult age (≥18 years)
- Patients identified in phase 1 with: 
      - Echocardiographically documented LVH (wall thickness ≥13 mm)
      - High DL-based probability of cardiac amyloidosis (top 110 us2.ai score)
- No evidence of definitive further cardiac amyloidosis diagnostics (e.g., no previous CMR, scintigraphy, biopsy, or genetic diagnostics)
- Willingness to participate in the study and to undergo a cardiac MRI
- Ability to give informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Phase 1 (retrospective phase):
- Age <18 years
- Objection to the use of clinical data for research purposes
- Missing or insufficient image quality
- Lack of confirmed diagnosis

Phase 2 (prospective phase):
- MRI contraindications (implants not compatible with MRI, severe renal insufficiency GFR<30 ml/min/1.73m², known gadolinium allergy)
- Known alternative diagnosis (e.g., genetically confirmed Fabry syndrome)
- Pregnancy
- Lack of written consent to participate in the study
